accounts.owner_or_project: NEAR Auth / FastAuth (built and operated by Peersyst per auth.near.org); heavy current traffic comes via sweat-relayer.near (see unresolved on Sweat)
accounts.what_it_does: Shared FastAuth contract: verifies an Auth0/guard-checked JWT (via jwt.fast-auth.near router) and then calls v1.signer.sign with path '<guard_id>#<sub>' on behalf of the user, so each web2 login deterministically controls one MPC-derived key.
accounts.target_chain_evidence: The derived key signs NEAR transactions: docs.near.org says the SDK returns an Ed25519 key by default, 'the same login always controls the same account'; a relayer broadcasts the signed tx. The contract also supports secp256k1/ecdsa (other chains) but our sample shows only Ed25519 (domain_id 1), consistent with NEAR-account signing. Exact account-id mapping (implicit account from the derived pubkey?) not confirmed from docs.

evidence.claim: fast-auth.near's eddsa sign path is guard_id#user and domain_id = contract's mpc_domain_id; calls mpc_contract .sign(request)
evidence.quote_or_value: path: format!("{}#{}", guard_id.clone(), user), domain_id: self.mpc_domain_id,

evidence.claim: guard_id must be 'jwt#GUARD_NAME' so full path = jwt#<guard>#<sub>; guard names here are issuer URLs (e.g. https://fastauth.swe.at)

accounts.owner_or_project: NEAR Omni Bridge (Near-One/omni-bridge, GitHub org Near-One)
accounts.what_it_does: Omni Bridge NEAR-side contract: on sign_transfer / log_metadata it calls v1.signer.sign with path 'bridge-1' and key_version 0 on a keccak256 payload of the transfer/metadata message, producing an MPC ECDSA signature that the destination-chain bridge contract verifies to release/mint tokens.
accounts.target_chain_evidence: Outbound NEAR->foreign-chain transfers all use Chain Signatures (README). Supported: Ethereum, Bitcoin, Zcash (light client + Chain Signatures), Solana, Base, BNB, Arbitrum (Wormhole + Chain Signatures). The sign request is legacy ECDSA (key_version 0, keccak256 payload) so the per-request destination chain is not visible in the request itself; it is inside transfer_message (recipient chain). Not determinable from sign calls alone.

evidence.claim: sign_transfer calls MPC signer with the path; payload = keccak256 of TransferMessagePayload (transfer_id, token_address, amount, recipient, fee_recipient, message)
log_metadata_callback also signs (token name/symbol/decimals MetadataPayload) with same path, used to deploy token on foreign chain
